;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Sudan]]ese [[List of heads of government of Sudan|Prime Minister]] [[Abdalla Hamdok]] survives an [[assassination]] attempt in [[Khartoum]]. No one has claimed responsibility. [https://www.haaretz.com/world-news/asia-and-australia/sudanese-prime-minister-survives-assassination-attempt-in-khartoum-1.8641821 (''Haaretz'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/mar/09/sudanese-pm-abdalla-hamdok-survives-assassination-attempt-reports (''The Guardian'')]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]], [[Politics of Afghanistan]]
**[[Ashraf Ghani]] is sworn in as the [[President of Afghanistan|President]] of the Islamic Republic of [[Afghanistan]] amidst a rocket attack claimed by [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]]. [[Abdullah Abdullah]] proclaims himself as President as well. [https://www.geo.tv/latest/276409-two-blasts-in-kabul-take-place-during-ashraf-ghanis-inauguration (AFP via Geo News)]
*[[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|Libyan Civil War]], [[Turkish military intervention in the Second Libyan Civil War]], [[2019–20 Western Libya offensive]]
**Nearly 40 [[Syrians|Syrian]] mercenaries recruited by the [[Turkish Army]] have fled to [[Italy]], raising the number of Syrian fighters who fled from Libya to Europe to nearly 200. [http://www.syriahr.com/en/?p=156666 (SOHR)]
*[[International military intervention against ISIL]]
**Two [[United States troops]] are killed in a raid against ISIL in [[Iraq]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/american-troops-killed-iraq-anti-isis-mission/story?id=69483422 (ABC)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[Black Monday (2020)|Black Monday]], [[2020 Russia–Saudi Arabia oil price war]]
***[[Price of oil|Oil prices]] plummet after [[Saudi Arabia]] cut its official selling prices over the weekend. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/03/08/investing/oil-prices-crash-opec-russia-saudi-arabia/index.html (CNN)]
***Before markets open, the [[Dow Jones Industrial Average]] futures posted a 1,300-point drop due to the coronavirus and a fall in the price of oil. The drop would be the [[List of largest daily changes in the Dow Jones Industrial Average|most points the Dow has dropped in a single day]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/business/business-news/dow-futures-tumble-1-000-points-all-out-oil-price-n1152716 (NBC News)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/business/markets/dow-set-open-decline-1-300-points-oil-war-adds-n1152941 (NBC News)]
***The [[Dow Jones Industrial Average]] plummets 1,800 points on opening, 500 points lower than pre-market futures trading. [https://www.msnbc.com/stephanie-ruhle/watch/stocks-plunge-at-market-open-trading-halts-after-dow-drops-1800-points-80319557862 (MSNBC)]
**[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
***The [[United Kingdom]]'s largest retailer [[Tesco]] say they will be restricting the sale of essential food and household items in response to fears of mass [[panic buying]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-51790375 (BBC News)] [https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/coronavirus-crisis-meeting-rationing-introduced-21656969 (''Daily Mirror'')]
**The [[2020 BNP Paribas Open]] (Indian Wells) is canceled due to coronavirus fears. This is one of the first major sporting events in the United States to be canceled over the coronavirus. [https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2879924-indian-wells-2020-canceled-amid-public-health-emergency-for-coronavirus (Bleacher Report)] [https://www.news.com.au/sport/tennis/paribas-open-cancelled-amid-coronavirus-fears/news-story/9a5c34588981a760cfc00cc90dbdda4f (News AU)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
****The number of confirmed cases in [[Italy]] rose to 9,172, while the death toll rose to 463. [https://www.corriere.it/salute/malattie_infettive/20_marzo_09/bollettino-coronavirus-9-marzo-regione-dati-provincia-ff355794-621d-11ea-9897-5c6f48cf812d_preview.shtml (''Corriere della Sera'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic lockdown in Italy]]
*****[[Prime Minister of Italy|Italian Prime Minister]] [[Giuseppe Conte]] extends the lockdown from Northern Italy to the whole country. [https://edition.cnn.com/2020/03/09/europe/coronavirus-italy-lockdown-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*****Riots continue at several prisons in Italy after family visitations were suspended due to the [[Coronavirus disease 2019|coronavirus]] pandemic. Inmates took two prison guards hostage in [[Modena]] during an attempted escape, while inmates at [[San Vittore Prison]] in [[Milan]] overpowered guards and occupied the roof. Prisons in [[Pavia]] and [[Rebibbia]] are set on fire, allowing some prisoners to escape. [https://www.businessinsider.com/inmates-riot-escape-from-italian-prisons-amid-coronavirus-restrictions-2020-3?r=US&IR=T (''Business Insider'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus]]
****The Minister of Health of [[Cyprus]] confirms the first two cases in the island; one a health professional who visited United Kingdom and the other a 25-year-old man who had traveled from Italy. [https://cyprus-mail.com/2020/03/09/two-cases-of-coronavirus-confirmed/ (''Cyprus Mail'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****The first two COVID-19 deaths are confirmed in [[Germany]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/world-51796781 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****The French [[Ministry of Culture (France)|Minister of Culture]] [[Franck Riester]] announces he is infected with [[COVID-19]], as five members of the [[National Assembly (France)|National Assembly]] join the 1,412 cases in the Republic. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-france/french-culture-minister-infected-by-coronavirus-but-is-well-source-idUSKBN20W2SM (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****The [[President of the Community of Madrid]] [[Isabel Díaz Ayuso]] orders the suspension of classes "at all educational levels" between 11 March until 30 March, as the region reports more than 500 cases. [https://www.lavanguardia.com/local/madrid/20200309/474061897680/madrid-ordena-cierre-colegios-coronavirus.html (''La Vanguardia'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] cancels all the [[Saint Patrick's Day]] parades. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-51806551 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****In order to combat the spread of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|coronavirus]], Israel orders all arrivals from abroad, regardless of country, to self-quarantine. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/israel-orders-all-arrivals-from-abroad-into-two-week-quarantine/ (''Times of Israel'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]]
****[[Saudi Arabia]] suspends all schools, universities and other educational institutions until further notice in response to the ongoing [[Coronavirus disease 2019|coronavirus]] pandemic. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/gulf/2020/03/08/Coronavirus-Saudi-Arabia-suspends-all-schools-universities-until-further-notice.html (Al Arabiya)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****The infection rate is reduced, but [[President of South Korea|South Korean president]] [[Moon Jae-in]] said it was "too early to be optimistic". [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/asia/coronavirus-south-korea-outbreak-cases-infections-deaths-a9387351.html (''The Independent'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Ted Cruz]] and [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] [[Paul Gosar]] self-quarantine themselves after having made contact at [[Conservative Political Action Conference|CPAC]] with a man confirmed to have been infected with COVID-19. [https://www.usatoday.com/amp/4996904002 (''USA Today'')]
***[[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Representative]] [[Matt Gaetz]] announces that he will quarantine for 14 days after making contact at the [[Conservative Political Action Conference|CPAC]] with a man who tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2020/03/07/matt-gaetz-coronavirus-florida/ (''The Washington Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic on cruise ships]]
****The ''[[Grand Princess]]'' cruise ship, with at least 21 people aboard who've tested positive for COVID-19, has docked at the [[Port of Oakland]], [[California]], to continue to the next step in the quarantining measures process. The ship was carrying more than 2,000 passengers, as well as 1,100 crew members. The Grand Princess had been idling about {{convert|10|miles|km}} offshore since Thursday (March 5). Disembarking American passengers are being put under mandatory 14-day quarantine at military bases in California, [[Texas]] or [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]]. Foreign passengers are being sent to their home countries for the completion of the quarantine. [https://www.foxnews.com/travel/grand-princess-cruise-ship-disembarking-oakland-port (Fox News)]

;International relations
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**[[North Korea]] fires three projectiles from the coast of [[Sondok Airport|Sondok]] into the sea, according to [[South Korea]]’s Joint Chiefs of Staff. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-missiles/north-korea-fires-three-projectiles-into-sea-china-urges-dialogue-idUSKBN20V14H (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*The [[United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit]] confirms a 2016 ruling that [[Led Zeppelin]]'s 1971 song "[[Stairway to Heaven]]" was not unlawfully [[Plagiarism|copied]] from [[Spirit (band)|Spirit]]'s [[instrumental]] "[[Taurus (instrumental)|Taurus]]", overturning the so-called [[Substantial similarity#Inverse ratio rule|inverse ratio rule]] [[Legal tests|test]]. [https://www.upi.com/Entertainment_News/Music/2020/03/09/Led-Zeppelin-prevails-in-Stairway-to-Heaven-copyright-case/5841583770503/ (UPI)]
